English: Watch Post
A makeshift lookout point, often a timber scaffold or a hastily raised earth mound, allowing sentries to spot threats from afar.
Signal Tower
A modest stone tower equipped with fire beacons, horns, and flags to relay warnings quickly to the surrounding countryside.
Guard Tower
A wooden guard tower with a raised platform, providing basic shelter for sentries and improved oversight of the castle approaches.
Flanking Tower
A robust stone flanking tower, projecting from the walls to allow defenders to sweep attackers with enfilading fire.
Arrow Tower
A tall, stone arrow tower with multiple firing slits, providing archers with excellent vantage points to rain arrows on besiegers.
Round Tower
A massive round stone tower with thick walls, designed to deflect siege engines and resist undermining, forming a formidable anchor in the defenses.
Holed Tower
A specialized tower with machicolations and murder holes, allowing defenders to pour boiling liquids and stones onto attackers below.
High Keep Tower
A towering stone keep rising above the castle, serving as both the last redoubt and a symbol of lordly might and prestige.
Bastion Tower
A cutting-edge bastion tower featuring angled walls for deflecting projectiles, internal barracks, and advanced defensive works, an evolution in fortification design.
Grand Turret
The ultimate expression of castle defense: a monumental turret with command chambers, artillery platforms, and living quarters for elite guards, a symbol of unassailable power.
